subject: ADR-209: the door has called it destructive since ADR-112, the page never asked, and the question had never been refused
body: Fifteen controls across this kit took TWO OR MORE OF YOUR RECORDS ON ONE TAP and asked nothing -- 'Clear trial' beside 'Add plot', on a phone, in a wet field, under a thumb. THE GATEWAY HAS RAISED DESTRUCTIVE ON THAT BUTTON SINCE ADR-112: a task must declare a rung to reach it, the outputs audit refuses to press it, and the risk ladder publishes it in its own argument pool. None of that classification ever reached the person doing the tapping. tools/audit_destructive.py is the kit's own rule asked of the page -- harness_plugin_page.destroys names the control, only kinds the door presses are candidates (ADR-208), the press happens with the page's own data in it, and the verdict is ASKS / NOTHING / ONE / BULK, with a ratchet downward per page and an exemption that needs a reason. ROWS ON THE SCREEN ARE NOT RECORDS, and the first draft proved it by being wrong in both directions at once: a plate shown once in its list and once in the results table built from it is ONE record counted twice, so a row remover read as a bulk delete; and a trait whose eighteen measurements live in a table the remove also empties read as the SAME SIZE as the row itself. A rule that cries wolf on a crossed-off chip is turned off within a week, and then the sheet-clearing ones are invisible again -- ADR-112's own warning arriving on a rule written a hundred slices later. So the audit asks the page WHAT IT IS HOLDING, through the autosave: the description the page already writes for every save and the outbox already checksums. KEEP 1.3.0 makes that handle reachable from outside the page's closure (KEEP.live()), because a page wires KEEP inside an IIFE and kept the only description of its own state in a local. A page with no autosave falls back to the screen AND SAYS WHICH READING IT IS, because a rule that silently measured nothing on such a page would report every one of them clean. A record is an element of an array the page keeps, or a form field with something typed in it -- not the fields INSIDE a record, which made an Undo that pops one measurement read as taking five, and not arrays alone, because the ethogram's kappa pane keeps two observers' sequences in two textareas and no array at all. WHAT ONE TAP WAS TAKING: the breeding bench's trial, the cell bench's standard curve and mitotic count, the cp and soil benches' mixes, the soil bench's pile, the ethogram's two sequences and agreement matrix, the greenhouse's reading log (whose sibling 'Clear every saved run?' has asked since it was written), the micro bench's growth curve, the ordination matrix, the field notebook's quadrats, the survey's target list, and Start over on BOTH tracks of the experiment guide. THREE DELETES CASCADED IN SILENCE: removing a plant from the cp bench took nine observations, removing a trait from the selection log took EIGHTEEN typed measurements, and removing an individual took its measurements and its pedigree links -- each row displayed the count and none of them said it was attached. Every confirmation NAMES WHAT GOES AND HOW MANY, because 'Are you sure?' is a question nobody reads. AND THE BUTTON THAT REMOVED THE BACKUP WAS REMOVING THE ORIGINAL: 'Forget this device's copy' on the experiment guide blanked the design on the screen as well, seventeen records to a button whose label promises only that a saved copy stops existing; every other page in this kit leaves the working state alone. ONE EXEMPTION, WRITTEN DOWN: the ethogram's Undo keeps a stack in its autosave, so a press takes two things from the description while the person loses one. AND ONE THE FULL RUN FOUND: two page suites went red the moment the confirmations landed, because HEADLESS CHROMIUM DISMISSES AN UNHANDLED DIALOG -- so a suite that presses Clear and asserts the sheet is empty would otherwise have passed only because the page never got to ask. Fourteen suites now answer the questions the pages ask.  AND THE QUESTION ITSELF IS NOW WATCHED: the harness's stub answers confirm() with TRUE, which is what makes the loss measurable, and it also meant the rule above only ever watched the YES path -- a page can ask, ignore the answer and destroy anyway, which reads as ASKS and is WORSE than never asking, because a question the page does not mean teaches the person that every question on it is noise. Every control that asks is pressed TWICE now, yes and no, and one that takes records on the no path is IGNORES, on the worklist beside the ones that never asked. NO PAGE IN THIS KIT DOES IT -- all twenty-one that ask honour the answer -- so the rule is driven against a DEFIANT FIXTURE: two buttons that both ask, both take three records on yes, and differ only in whether the answer means anything. ADR-127's point about a refusal nobody has watched and ADR-207's about a rule with nothing left to catch, arriving together on the confirmations this slice added. AN UNDO CASCADES TOO, AND THE CORRECTED INSTRUMENT FOUND IT: the selection log's iUndo takes the last individual and every measurement and pedigree link that names it, which is what undoing an add has to mean -- but Undo is the word a person presses without reading, and it was taking measurements typed long after the add it reverses. It read as a one-record remover until the audit stopped carrying the previous page's autosave into the measurement. AND THE AUDIT WAS MEASURING ITS OWN HISTORY: one control is pressed per page and every page shared one browser context, so the autosave ADR-207 gave these pages carried a sheet from the previous measurement into the next, and the same button read as taking three records on one run and six on another depending on how many pages had been opened before it; storage is cleared before each page's own scripts run, because clearing after load would race the restore (ADR-155's defect, on browser storage instead of on a fill counter). verify_destructive 44 over three fixtures, one that keeps its state and shows every row twice, one that keeps nothing at all and one that asks and ignores the answer; it pins that the multiplication sign in 'Copy host x taxon matrix' is not a delete, that a text box whose label says clear is not a control anybody taps, that three records are three and not six, that a typed field is a record, that asking does not stop the loss being measured (the stub answers confirm with true, and a rule that stopped at 'it asked' would not know whether asking stopped anything), and that before - after == loss on every row. mutate_destructive 30 all killed, mutate_keep 30 -> 32 all killed, verify_keep 282 -> 316, verify_br 87 -> 90. ONE MORE THE CLOSE FOUND: verify_board refused the render, because the board's table of mutant runners is a SECOND LIST -- ADR-141's shape once more, this time caught the same day by the check written for it. 0 of 95 destructive controls take two or more records on one tap and ask nothing; twenty-one now ask, thirty-three take exactly one, and twenty-five pages carry a ceiling of zero.
